title: pilot-proposal-grove-insurance-scrapbook
notes:
Context: quick personal scratchpad for an initial outbound / pilot proposal to Grove Insurance (regional insurer focused on SME commercial policies). Not polished — use as a working source for calls, emails, and a lightweight pilot brief.

Account snapshot:
- Name: Grove Insurance Co. (midwest regional; ~$250M revenue).
- Why them: heavy underwriting volume, rapid claim triage needs, interest in AI to speed adjuster workflows. Public statements about automation & developer partnerships in Q2 investor deck.
- Likely buyers: Head of Digital (Elena Park — LinkedIn), Head of Claims Ops (Tom Whitaker), Platform/Integration lead (API team).
- Security posture: PCI/PII consciousness, interested in private deployments for internal models (mentioned in RFP appendix).

Primary hypothesis for outreach:
- Use Redwood Private or Dedicated for a 6-week pilot: accelerate claims triage (first-pass narrative summarization + suggested next-step actions) and reduce manual triage time by ~30%.
- Value props to lead with: predictable latency under heavy bursts, VPC/private control for PII, cost predictability for per-claim processing, built-in evaluation to track quality regressions vs human baseline.

Pilot outline (6 weeks) — MVP scope:
- Week 0: NDA + data readiness call. Agree on 500–2,000 anonymized claim snippets.
- Week 1: Ingest pipeline (S3 or secure upload) + quick model selection (open LLM small-medium recommended).
- Week 2–3: Map prompts + create evaluation rubric (precision for recommended action; recall for flagged high-risk claims).
- Week 4: Internal beta: 1000 live-inbox items routed through Redwood endpoint (shadowing). Latency SLO: p95 < 700ms for typical payload (300 tokens).
- Week 5: Feedback loop: sample human review + quality dashboard.
- Week 6: Pilot review, cost/latency report, recommendation for phase 1 roll-out.

Key technical asks from Grove (to clarify on discovery):
- Max acceptable latency per request and spike tolerance.
- Data residency requirements (EU? on-prem?).
- Allowed outbound model updates and retention windows for logs/cache.
- Preferred auth/KMS integrations (Azure KeyVault, AWS KMS, Hashicorp).

Outbound email draft (short):
Subject: Pilot idea to reduce claims triage time at Grove
Hi Elena — quick note from Riley at Redwood. We help infra + product teams run low-latency, private LLM inference with predictable cost (think: private API + rollout controls for production). I reviewed Grove's Q2 notes on automation and had a small pilot idea: a 6-week shadow pilot that routes a sample of claim narratives through a private Redwood endpoint and shows head-to-head time and quality delta vs baseline reviewers. No production changes, we handle ingestion and evaluation, and we can sign an NDA up front. Would you be open to a 20–30 minute discovery?
Best, Riley

Call agenda (20–30 min):
1) Quick intros + objectives (3 min)
2) Current claim triage flow + pain points (7 min)
3) Data access + security constraints (5 min)
4) Pilot mechanics + success metrics (3 min)
5) Next steps / timelines (2 min)

Objection handling notes (short bullets):
- "We can’t risk PII exposure": propose Private deployment + customer-managed KMS + audit logs + ephemeral KV cache. Offer code-level access review and an on-prem option if required.
- "Not sure LLM quality will match our standards": commit to evaluation plan with blind human comparison, acceptance thresholds, and rollback rules. Suggest a canary within a non-critical region.
- "Cost concerns": show example unit economics (estimates): 0.8s p95, average tokens 350 -> cost X per claim; pilot costs capped and transparent. Offer a shared cost model for the pilot.
- "Ops burden": Redwood handles model updates, runtime, and monitoring for pilot; propose a biweekly check-in cadence and a single SE contact.

Unresolved questions for discovery (write down during call):
- Who owns the decision for pilots (procurement vs. Head of Digital vs Claims Ops)?
- Are there existing vendor risk questionnaires (VRQ) or SOC2 requirements we should complete first?
- Can they provide a de-identified sample set this quarter? Format + size?
- What is their expected timeline for a vendor POC -> production (3 months? 6 months?)

Quick ROI back-of-envelope to bring to call:
- If average manual triage time = 5.5 min/claim, 30% reduction -> 1.65 min saved/claim. At 20k claims/month -> 33k minutes saved (~550 hours). At $60/hr fully-burdened -> ~$33k/month potential savings.
- Emphasize non-monetary value: faster SLAs, fewer escalations, better adjuster morale.

Next steps (my TODOs):
- Find Elena Park contact email + confirm org chart ownership (Due: 2025-09-18) — Anika to help.
- Draft short pilot SOW + example NDA (template) (Due: 2025-09-20) — Riley.
- Create JIRA ticket for pilot infra provisioning requirements (JIRA-8431) and link to Confluence page.
- Prep a 2-slide one-pager for CEO + Head of Claims if requested.

Notes to self: keep the first pilot scope very narrow. Avoid promise of 100% automation — sell measurable lift and safe failure modes. Use Dedicated capacity if they care about peak throughput; Private if they require VPC/HSM.

Simple versions of metrics to commit to in pilot:
- Quality: human-validated accept rate >= 85% for recommended actions.
- Latency: p95 < 700ms for standard payload; p99 < 1500ms optional.
- Cost: pilot capped at $X (fill after infra quote).
